title: Nestor (Mauricio) Collado
text:
PhD Candidate
Bren School of Environmental Science & Management
University of California, Santa Barbara





I am a PhD candidate in Environmental Economics at the Bren School of Environmental Science & Management at the University of California, Santa Barbara. I study how regulators should design environmental and resource policy instruments (taxes, quotas, and bundles of them) when information about the underlying system is limited and outcomes are uncertain, with applications to renewable and non-renewable resources. In these cases, regulators cannot finely target behavior, goods, or bads. My research asks how relatively coarse instruments can still improve environmental and economic outcomes under uncertainty.

Research Themes

Environmental and Resource Economics
My work examines extraction, and resource management under uncertainty.


Environmental policy under limited information
I study how information constraints shape the choice between taxes, quotas, and broader policy bundles.


Applied Microeconomics Theory
I rely on dynamic economic models to understand regulation when ecosystems are complex and policy must remain feasible in practice.

Perú Crecimiento Verde: Análisis Cuantitativo de Políticas Verdes en Sectores Seleccionados de la Economía
Néstor Mauricio Collado Duran; Elsa Galarza; Bruno Seminario De Marzi; Daniel de la Torre Ugarte; Maria Alejandra Zegarra

  



Summary

This study evaluates the impact of green policies in the forestry, urban transport, and agriculture sectors in the year 2035. It uses the Millennium Institute’s T-21 model for quantitative analysis, integrating economic, social, and environmental dimensions. The results suggest that green policies can contribute to reducing greenhouse gases, though economic and social benefits vary across sectors.




Perú Crecimiento Verde: Análisis de la Economía Peruana
Néstor Mauricio Collado Duran; Elsa Galarza; Bruno Seminario De Marzi; Daniel de la Torre Ugarte; Maria Alejandra Zegarra

  



Summary

This document has three objectives: to summarize relevant information and analyze political indicators and trends that can guide the PAGE initiative’s intervention in Peru; to lay the groundwork for a second quantitative assessment of green economy policies in key sectors; and to establish the basis for developing a green growth strategy and discussing it with relevant stakeholders.

title: Peer-Reviewed Publications
text:
Note: I publish under both N. Collado and M. Collado

Indexing Spatio-temporal Maritime Trajectories for Route Prediction
Siya Qiu; Yihong Luo; Mauricio Collado; Qiong Luo; Jing Tang

  



Abstract

Maritime trajectory modeling is crucial for ensuring the safety and efficiency of maritime transportation. However, the unique challenges of the open ocean, such as the lack of a pre-determined road network and infrequent vessel interactions, render traditional land-based route prediction systems inadequate. To overcome these obstacles, we present ST-Shape, a spatio-temporal trajectory indexing method designed to swiftly retrieve pertinent historical maritime trajectories, thereby facilitating long-term trajectory prediction. ST-Shape approximates trajectories using two-dimensional polygons and constructs the index with shape indices, thus preserving the spatio-temporal properties of each trajectory. Concurrently, we introduce a straightforward yet robust model that harnesses this indexed data to predict vessel movements. To underpin our research, we have curated a comprehensive maritime trajectory dataset from the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, classified according to diverse navigational scenarios. Our endeavor serves as a foundational step towards expedited spatio-temporal trajectory retrieval for maritime trajectory prediction, marking a significant stride in enhancing maritime safety and navigational efficiency.



A Deep Decarbonization Pathway for Peru’s Rainforest
Daniel De La Torre Ugarte; Mauricio Collado; Fernando Requejo; Ximena Gomez; Carlos Heros

  



Abstract

Peru holds an important portion of the South American rainforest. An average deforestation rate of 145,000 hectares per year makes it the largest source of greenhouse gas emissions. Based on the drivers of deforestation, this paper proposes a deep decarbonization pathway through the year 2050 with the purpose of taking the country closer to achieving the net-zero emissions goal. The impacts of the pathway are estimated using POLYSYS-Peru, an equilibrium displacement model for the integrated analysis of land-use changes and agriculture. The results indicate that the proposed pathway, by preventing the deforestation of 4 million hectares of primary forests, would reduce greenhouse gas emissions substantially relative to business as usual and beyond the Nationally Determined Contributions.



Net-zero Deep Decarbonization Pathways in Latin America: Challenges and Opportunities
Christopher Bataille; Henri Waisman; Yann Briand; Johannes Svensson; Adrien Vogt-Schilb; Marcela Jaramillo; Ricardo Delgado; Ricardo Arguello; Leon Clarke; Thomas Wild; Francisco Lallana; Gonzalo Bravo; Gustavo Nadal; Gaëlle Le Treut; Guido Godinez; Jairo Quiros-Tortos; Eunice Pereira; Mark Howells; Daniel Buira; Jordi Tovilla; Jamil Farbes; Jones Ryan; Daniel De La Torre Ugarte; Mauricio Collado; Fernando Requejo; Ximena Gomez; Rafael Soria; Daniel Villamar; Pedro Rochedo; Mariana Imperio

  



Abstract

This synthesis paper presents the objectives, approach, and cross-cutting results of the Latin American Deep Decarbonization Pathways project. It synthesizes and compares detailed national and sectoral pathways to 2050 compatible with the Paris Agreement objectives and domestic development priorities in Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Mexico, and Peru. It derives insights for the design of domestic policy packages and identifies priorities for international cooperation.



Evaluation of Early Action Mechanisms in Peru Regarding Preparedness for El Niño
Julio Aguirre; Daniel De La Torre Ugarte; Juan Bazo; Paulo Quequezana; Mauricio Collado

  



Abstract

This article provides an impact evaluation of an intervention in Peru regarding preparedness for El Niño impacts in Picsi District of Chiclayo Province in Peru’s northwestern coastal Lambayeque region. The intervention involved the provision of special kits that reduce potential damage to homes as a consequence of rainfall and floods associated with an El Niño-Southern Oscillation event. Using propensity score matching techniques, the study finds a positive impact of the program in mitigating house damage.



Examination of the Peruvian Anchovy Individual Vessel Quota (IVQ) System
Kailin Kroetz; James N. Sanchirico; Elsa Galarza Contreras; David Corderi Novoa; Nestor Collado; Elaine W. Swiedler

  



Abstract

This paper examines changes following the implementation of a catch share system in the Peruvian anchovy fishery, the world’s largest commercial fishery by volume. After implementation of the IVQ management system, there was a shift toward higher value product, more fishing days, fleet consolidation over time, and higher variable harvesting profit.



Fishing Rights: The Case of the Peruvian Anchoveta Fishery
Elsa Galarzar; Nestor Collado


Abstract

The implementation in 2009 of maximum catch limits per vessel in the industrial anchoveta fishery engendered a series of changes in fisheries management. This research estimates resource rent for the industrial anchoveta fishery for 2011, compares effort under open access and the quota regime, and discusses the current payment for fishing rights along with private sector contributions.

title: Research
text:
Work in Progress

Prices vs. Quantities Under Complex Constraints
Extends Weitzman’s (1974) instrument-choice framework to a multi-good static setting in which regulated goods are correlated through non-separable benefits (substitutes or complements) and jointly distributed cost and benefit shocks.


Weak Property Rights and Resource Extraction
Shows that heterogeneity in firms’ effective discount rates—capturing institutional risk and weak property rights—generates accelerated extraction and distortions of the classic Hotelling path in a competitive non-renewable resource market.


Aggregate Quotas under Depletion Risk (with Shu-chen Tsao)
Considers a setting in which a regulator cannot distinguish species at port and therefore sets a single aggregate quota, while one species within that aggregate requires near-zero harvest to recover; characterizes the socially optimal aggregate quota under this constraint.

title: Teaching
text:
Teaching Assistant, Spring 2026 This course reviews the key concepts and tools of corporate financial management and reporting and environmental accounting.
As a teaching assistant, I helped design assignments that asked students to search for real data and use the tools in R, Excel or any software of their preference. I gave lecture sharing my experience in the stock market.



Teaching Assistant, Fall 2023, Fall 2024, Fall 2025
This course examines the economic theory of environmental policy, with particular emphasis on cost-benefit analysis and methods for valuing non-market environmental goods. Topics include ecosystem protection, pollution control, and applied tools for environmental decision-making.
As a teaching assistant, I helped design assignments that asked students to replicate and adapt peer-reviewed papers using R. I also advised students on their term projects, many of which were connected to their graduate group projects.



Teaching Assistant, Spring 2024, Winter 2025, Winter 2026
This course provides a foundation in environmental economics, focusing on the causes of environmental problems and the economic tools available to address them. It covers topics such as externalities, climate change, renewable resource management, and the distributional consequences of environmental harms and policy responses.
As a teaching assistant, I helped redesign the course each quarter to fit the backgrounds and professional goals of students from diverse fields. I also contributed to assignments that balanced economic theory, quantitative reasoning, and coding.

Teaching Assistant, 2012 The course aims to study, at an intermediate level, the role of the price mechanism in the allocation of scarce resources, with a partial equilibrium approach.

title: Research
text:
Job Market Paper

Bundle Fisheries Under Ecological Uncertainty

 PDF

Abstract: Many fisheries cannot be regulated one species at a time, and some fisheries manage multiple stocks under a single economic instrument. I study when such bundling is desirable and whether it should take the form of a shared quota or a shared landing fee (tax), extending the constant-escapement framework of Reed (1979) and Weitzman (2002) to a multispecies fishery under ecological uncertainty.
The central condition for a well-designed basket is equalizing marginal profits across species, a condition that combines biological productivity, harvesting costs, and prices. Under this criterion, both instruments are first-best when shocks are deterministic, but under uncertainty both become second-best, with the tax outperforming the quota. The main reason for this difference is that the quota must be set before shocks are realized. As the basket grows, the quota’s disadvantage is diversified away, but a second cost, the mismatch from pooling heterogeneous species, grows with basket size. Larger baskets are not always better.
Bundling improves on species-specific management only when the monitoring costs it saves exceed this pooling loss.
